Composition of instruction text by function (12-code codebook, share of characters); request size growth; relative edit size (Levenshtein) per transition; segments added/removed/modified; share of change units explaining the stack change (yes/indirectly/no) and motivation categories; shared segments across agents (verbatim and near-duplicate)

Automatic capture via local HTTP server intercepting the first request to the main model, in fresh containers; automatic segmentation and diffs. Coding: GLM 5.3 Flash (via OpenRouter) validated against two human coders (human kappa 0.75; LLM 93.4% agreement, kappa 0.92). Tracing: mini-swe-agent with Gemini 4 Argon, validated on 55 transitions (795/798 links correct); motivation coding by Gemini 4 Argon, kappa >= 0.82 vs reference

N/A as an approach evaluation (no task, success criterion or quality/cost verdict). Agents run only to capture requests, with default or fixed models: (1) Claude Code + default model: 493/494 captured; tool definitions 77.4% of latest request; directive share fell to 54% after 2.1.154. (2) Codex CLI + o4-mini (to 0.19.0) then gpt-5: 174/175; request grew x7.8. (3) Gemini CLI + default model: 192/192; x1.4. (4) OpenCode + gpt-5: 907/930 (15 failed to initialise provider); size shrank ~25%. (5) Qwen Code + qwen3-coder-plus: 120/120; x4.5

Cross-agent descriptive comparison: 5 agents, all stable npm releases before 25 Aug 2026; held constant: fixed user prompt, fresh linux/amd64 container, empty working directory, default settings except endpoint redirection and model selection; one run per release; no human intervention; no baseline (descriptive)

Directive text 89-96% (median) of instruction text in all agents; tool definitions dominate Claude Code, Qwen Code, OpenCode latest requests (77.4%, 72.3%, 63.2%); 29% of transitions change a segment or tool, 5-10 transitions account for half of edits; only 48% of 496 units explain the stack change itself; safety cited by 13 units; by Aug 2026 >= 95% of each agent's segments unique; four open-source agents converge in directive share (84-87%). Descriptive; no significance tests

Distinguished agents descriptively; capture repeatable (fixed configuration, hashes stored, replication package). Limitations: first request only, empty directory, no user customisation or later turns; stated motivations may differ from actual; LLM-assisted annotation errors possible

Construct: stated, not verified, motivations. Internal: labelling errors from human/LLM annotation. External: five CLI agents, controlled configuration, first request only, no repository guidance or later interactions; releases before 25 Aug 2026. Effects on correctness, tool use, latency, cost not established; future: controlled experiments varying stacks with fixed model/task, ablations, capturing later turns. Recommends reporting exact agent release and archiving captured stacks

Relevant to SDD only indirectly: argues the agent release is an experimental variable and that repository guidance (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) operates inside the instruction stack. Reporting inconsistency: 25 of 1,911 releases not captured, but the text explains only 22 (15 OpenCode provider failures + 7 broken packages, p. 5); Table I gives 23 OpenCode, 1 Claude Code, 1 Codex missing. Fig. 3 table values partly jumbled by pdftotext (latest-release column); medians in text used. Replication package (anonymous 4open.science link) [1]. Codex switched from TypeScript to Rust implementation. No pre-registration
